Title: Diagnosis of test `testMath280()` failure in `NormalDistributionImpl.inverseCumulativeProbability`

Details:
- The test `testMath280()` initializes a `NormalDistribution` instance with mean 0 and standard deviation 1 using `NormalDistributionImpl(0,1)` (line 168).
- It then calls `inverseCumulativeProbability` with a probability value `0.9772498680518209`.
- In the `NormalDistributionImpl` class, the method `inverseCumulativeProbability(double p)` returns `Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY` if `p == 0`, returns `Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY` if `p == 1`, else it delegates to the superclass method with `super.inverseCumulativeProbability(p)` (lines 153-163).
- The constructor `NormalDistributionImpl(double mean, double sd)` sets the mean and standard deviation via setters (lines 53-57).
- The setters simply assign the passed mean and standard deviation values to private fields after validation for the standard deviation being greater than 0 (mean and standardDeviation fields).
- The mean field defaults to 0, and the standard deviation must be positive to not throw an exception.
- The issue likely resides within the `super.inverseCumulativeProbability(p)` method called by `NormalDistributionImpl.inverseCumulativeProbability`.
- Since `NormalDistributionImpl` extends `AbstractRealDistribution` (inferred from commons-math library structure) which may provide the inverse CDF implementation or delegate it further, the failure is possibly due to an incorrect or missing approximation implementation in the parent class.
- Without the parent class method details, a plausible cause is that `super.inverseCumulativeProbability` does not work correctly or throws an exception for this input probability `0.9772498680518209`.

Next steps:
- Check the code of the superclass method `inverseCumulativeProbability(double)` used by `NormalDistributionImpl`.
- Also investigate if there is any relevant exception handling or condition around the inversion logic in the superclass.

Suggested methods to investigate/fix:
- `org.apache.commons.math.distribution.NormalDistributionImpl.inverseCumulativeProbability(double)`
- `org.apache.commons.math.distribution.AbstractRealDistribution.inverseCumulativeProbability(double)` (or whichever superclass implements or overrides this method)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
